claim: The payment page serves any invoice by its counting number with no sign-in, so access to an invoice is not tied to anyone's permission to see it.
Nothing states that the billing app keeps a user's reads and writes inside their own company: it loads invoices by number, adds the tenant filter by hand, and the database enforces no tenant rule.
notes: Whether the check exists is a property of the app's code.

claim: The only stated role control is hiding buttons in the pages; nothing states that the server checks the role on each request.
notes: A client-side control is stated and a server-side one is not.

claim: The billing app saves every field an edit posts, so no field is restricted to the users allowed to change it.
notes: Stated outright: the paid flag and the payout bank account included.

claim: Nobody wrote down who may read or change which invoices, beyond an admin and viewer role.
notes: A fuller description could state the rules; the source names the roles and nothing they allow.

claim: Nobody wrote down which invoice fields each role may read or change.
The edit handler accepts every field it receives rather than a list of fields each action allows.
notes: Stated outright; the same fact as V8.2.3 read as a coding defect.

claim: Nobody wrote down that PDF rendering is resource-demanding or how its load is limited.
notes: The source states the opposite of a limit: any user, any invoice, as often as they like.

claim: Users, admins included, sign in with a password alone.
notes: Stated outright: no second factor for admins or viewers.

claim: When a support agent acts as a customer user, the record names the customer user and not the agent who acted.
